title: What Is a Chat Mixer on a Gaming Headset
summary: Learn what a chat mixer does on a gaming headset, how to balance game audio and chat volume on Xbox, PS5, and PC, and which headsets have one built in.
body_markdown:
You are mid-match. Explosions rattle the screen, the soundtrack is cranked, and your teammate is calling out a flanker on your six. You catch none of it. Or it goes the other way, and their callout drowns out the footsteps behind you.


A chat mixer solves that problem. Here is what a chat mixer actually does, how to use one on every platform, and why some


[gaming headsets](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/headsets) handle the job better than others.


### Quick Answer


A chat mixer controls the balance between game audio and voice chat. On Xbox, open the Guide and go to Audio. On PS5, adjust the Game/Chat slider under Sound. On PC, use the system Volume Mixer or Discord settings. Wireless headsets like the Stealth 700 Gen 3 include a game/chat dial on the ear cup for instant adjustments.


## How Does a Chat Mixer Work?


A chat mixer adjusts the balance between game audio and voice chat in real time. Instead of both sources playing at a fixed ratio, you slide the mix toward whichever one matters more right now.


- Slide toward game audio to bring up in-game sound effects, footsteps, and music


- Slide toward chat to boost your teammates' voices relative to the game


The overall volume stays roughly the same. You are just shifting how much of each source comes through. Most headsets offer either a physical dial on the ear cup or a software slider in your console settings.


## How to Use Chat Mixer on Xbox


Xbox has a chat mixer built right into the system. Here is how to find it:


1. Press the Xbox button to open the Guide


2. Go to the Audio section


3. Adjust the Headset chat mixer slider to balance game and chat volume


You can also reach the same control through Settings > General > Volume & Audio Output. The slider works with any headset connected via controller or USB, so even a basic


[wired headset](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/recon-70-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Black) gets access. New to the process? Our


[headset setup on Xbox](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/use-headset-on-xbox-setup-guide) guide has you covered.


Premium wireless headsets go further. The


[Stealth 700 Gen 3](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-700-gen-3-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Black) puts a game/chat mix dial on the ear cup, so you can rebalance audio without opening any menus. If your


[headset is not working on Xbox](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/headset-not-working-on-xbox) at all, troubleshoot the connection before tweaking the mixer.


## How to Use Chat Mixer on PlayStation


PS5 has a similar feature in its quick menu:


1. Press the PlayStation button


2. Select Sound


3. Adjust the Balance between Game and Chat audio slider


Companion apps like Swarm II can add more granular control on top of the console slider. If you need help getting


[a wireless headset connected to PS5](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/connect-wireless-headset-ps5) , start there before adjusting the mix.


Platform note:


Onboard game/chat mix dials on the Stealth 700 Gen 3 and


[Stealth 500](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-500-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Black) control game/chat balance on Xbox. On PlayStation and PC, the same dial defaults to mic monitoring or volume control instead.


****


## How to Balance Audio on PC


PC gives you the most flexibility, with several options that work alone or together:


System volume mixer:


Right-click the speaker icon in the taskbar, open Volume Mixer, and adjust individual app volumes so your game and voice chat are balanced.


In-game settings:


Many games have separate sliders for music, sound effects, and voice chat.


Headset companion apps:


Swarm II offers a dedicated chat mix slider alongside EQ presets and mic adjustments. Most


[wireless headsets with PC and console compatibility](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/wireless-headset-pc-console-compatibility) support it.


Discord per-user volume:


Right-click any user in your Discord voice channel to raise or lower their individual output.


## Why Can You Not Hear Your Friends Over Game Sound?


The most common culprits:


- Your chat mixer is set too far toward game audio


- Your voice chat app's volume sits lower than your game


- Your headset defaults to game-priority audio on first connection


- The person speaking has a


[muffled or quiet microphone](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/headset-mic-sounds-muffled-fix)


Start by checking your chat mixer balance. On Xbox, open the Guide and check the Audio slider. On PS5, check Game/Chat balance in the quick menu. On PC, compare Discord's output volume against the game.


If


[audio keeps cutting out](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/audio-cutting-out-in-games) or sounds distorted, make sure your headset firmware is current and the connection is solid. A


[crackling headset](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/headphones-crackling-fixes-guide) is typically a hardware or connection issue, not a mixer problem.


## Does Every Gaming Headset Have a Chat Mixer?


No. Wired headsets that plug in via 3.5mm do not include a standalone chat mixer control. You rely on your console or PC system settings.


Mid-range and premium wireless headsets are more likely to include a physical chat mix dial on the ear cup. The


[Stealth 600](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-600-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Purple) puts game/chat mix control on the lower ear cup for Xbox, while the


[Stealth Pro II](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-pro-ii-headset?Platform=Xbox&Color=Black) handles mixing through its base station. Having that control on your head means zero menu digging mid-firefight.

## Is a Headset Without a Chat Mixer Mono?


No. Chat mixer and audio channels are completely separate. A headset without a chat mixer still plays full stereo audio. Stereo output is determined by the headset's drivers, not a balance dial.


## Get the Right Chat Mix for Your Setup


A chat mixer gives you real-time control over the balance between game sound and voice chat, so you get both at the levels you want.


For the best onboard chat mixer on Xbox, the Stealth 700 Gen 3's remappable dial is hard to beat. Reassign that wheel to game/chat mix, mic monitoring, or bass boost through Swarm II. The Stealth 500 and Stealth 600 deliver the same core dial at lower price points.


Browse the full


[Xbox headsets](https://www.turtlebeach.com/collections/xbox-headsets) lineup, or check out our breakdown of


[wired and wireless options](https://www.turtlebeach.com/blog/should-i-stick-with-wired-or-try-wireless-gaming-headsets) if you have not picked a side yet.


## FAQs


### What does the chat mixer control on my headset actually do?


A chat mixer adjusts the volume balance between game audio and voice chat. You can make teammates louder or quieter relative to in-game sound without changing overall volume.


### How do I adjust game audio and chat volume separately?


On Xbox, use the Audio section in the Guide. On PS5, use the Game/Chat slider in the Sound quick menu. On PC, use the system volume mixer or your voice chat app settings.


### Is my headset mono if it does not have a chat mixer?


No. Chat mixer is a volume balance feature, not an audio format feature. Headsets without a chat mixer still output stereo audio through left and right drivers.


### Why can I not hear my friends over game sound?


Your chat mixer is probably set too far toward game audio. Check your console's audio balance slider or headset controls and shift the balance toward chat.


### Does every gaming headset have a chat mixer control?


No. Wired 3.5mm headsets usually rely on console-level settings. Wireless headsets are more likely to include a physical chat mixer dial on the ear cup.


### How do I use chat mixer on Xbox?


Press the Xbox button, go to Audio, and adjust the Headset chat mixer slider. You can also access the same control in Settings > General > Volume & Audio Output.
